doc: For non-zero `n : ℕ`, the ring `Fin n` is equivalent to `ZMod n`.
statement: (n : ℕ) → [NeZero n] → Fin n ≃+* ZMod n

doc:
`val a` is a natural number defined as:
- for `a : ZMod 0` it is the absolute value of `a`
- for `a : ZMod n` with `0 < n` it is the least natural number in the equivalence class

See `ZMod.valMinAbs` for a variant that takes values in the integers.
statement: {n : ℕ} → ZMod n → ℕ
∀ {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : ZMod n), a.val < n
∀ {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : ZMod n), a.val ≤ n
∀ {n : ℕ}, ZMod.val 0 = 0
ZMod.val 1 = 1
∀ {n : ZMod 0}, (-n).val = n.val
∀ {m n : ZMod 0}, (m * n).val = m.val * n.val
∀ (n a : ℕ), (↑a).val = a % n
∀ {n a : ℕ}, a < n → (↑a).val = a
∀ (n a : ℕ) [inst : a.AtLeastTwo], (OfNat.ofNat a).val = OfNat.ofNat a % n
∀ {n a : ℕ} [inst : a.AtLeastTwo], a < n → (OfNat.ofNat a).val = OfNat.ofNat a
∀ {n : ZMod 0}, IsUnit n ↔ n.val = 1
∀ {n : ℕ}, IsUnit ↑n → n = 1
∀ (n : ℕ), addOrderOf 1 = n

doc:
This lemma works in the case in which `ZMod n` is not infinite, i.e. `n ≠ 0`.  The version
where `a ≠ 0` is `addOrderOf_coe'`.
statement: ∀ (a : ℕ) {n : ℕ}, n ≠ 0 → addOrderOf ↑a = n / n.gcd a

doc:
This lemma works in the case in which `a ≠ 0`.  The version where
`ZMod n` is not infinite, i.e. `n ≠ 0`, is `addOrderOf_coe`.
statement: ∀ {a : ℕ} (n : ℕ), a ≠ 0 → addOrderOf ↑a = n / n.gcd a

doc: We have that `ringChar (ZMod n) = n`.
statement: ∀ (n : ℕ), ringChar (ZMod n) = n

doc:
Cast an integer modulo `n` to another semiring.
This function is a morphism if the characteristic of `R` divides `n`.
See `ZMod.castHom` for a bundled version.
statement: {R : Type u_1} → [AddGroupWithOne R] → {n : ℕ} → ZMod n → R
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : AddGroupWithOne R], ZMod.cast 0 = 0
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : AddGroupWithOne R] [NeZero n] (a : ZMod n), a.cast = ↑a.val

∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : AddGroupWithOne R] {S : Type u_2} [inst_1 : AddGroupWithOne S] (a : ZMod n),
  a.cast.1 = a.cast

∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : AddGroupWithOne R] {S : Type u_2} [inst_1 : AddGroupWithOne S] (a : ZMod n),
  a.cast.2 = a.cast

doc:
So-named because the coercion is `Nat.cast` into `ZMod`. For `Nat.cast` into an arbitrary ring,
see `ZMod.natCast_val`.
statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : ZMod n), ↑a.val = a
∀ {n : ℕ} [NeZero n], Function.RightInverse ZMod.val Nat.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} [NeZero n], Function.Surjective Nat.cast

doc:
So-named because the outer coercion is `Int.cast` into `ZMod`. For `Int.cast` into an arbitrary
ring, see `ZMod.intCast_cast`.
statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (a : ZMod n), ↑a.cast = a
∀ {n : ℕ}, Function.RightInverse ZMod.cast Int.cast
∀ {n : ℕ}, Function.Surjective Int.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} {P : ZMod n → Prop}, (∀ (x : ZMod n), P x) ↔ ∀ (x : ℤ), P ↑x
∀ {n : ℕ} {P : ZMod n → Prop}, (∃ x, P x) ↔ ∃ x, P ↑x
∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ZMod n), i.cast = i
∀ {n : ℕ}, ZMod.cast = id

doc: The coercions are respectively `Nat.cast` and `ZMod.cast`.
statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (R : Type u_1) [inst : Ring R] [NeZero n], Nat.cast ∘ ZMod.val = ZMod.cast

doc: The coercions are respectively `Int.cast`, `ZMod.cast`, and `ZMod.cast`.
statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (R : Type u_1) [inst : Ring R], Int.cast ∘ ZMod.cast = ZMod.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] [NeZero n] (i : ZMod n), ↑i.val = i.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] (i : ZMod n), ↑i.cast = i.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} (a b : ZMod n), (a + b).cast = if ↑n ≤ a.cast + b.cast then a.cast + b.cast - ↑n else a.cast + b.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {m : ℕ} [CharP R m], m ∣ n → ZMod.cast 1 = 1
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {m : ℕ} [CharP R m], m ∣ n → ∀ (a b : ZMod n), (a + b).cast = a.cast + b.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {m : ℕ} [CharP R m], m ∣ n → ∀ (a b : ZMod n), (a * b).cast = a.cast * b.cast

doc:
The canonical ring homomorphism from `ZMod n` to a ring of characteristic dividing `n`.

See also `ZMod.lift` for a generalized version working in `AddGroup`s.
statement: {n m : ℕ} → m ∣ n → (R : Type u_2) → [inst : Ring R] → [CharP R m] → ZMod n →+* R

∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {m : ℕ} [inst_1 : CharP R m] {h : m ∣ n} (i : ZMod n),
  (ZMod.castHom h R) i = i.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {m : ℕ} [CharP R m], m ∣ n → ∀ (a b : ZMod n), (a - b).cast = a.cast - b.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {m : ℕ} [CharP R m], m ∣ n → ∀ (a : ZMod n), (-a).cast = -a.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {m : ℕ} [CharP R m], m ∣ n → ∀ (a : ZMod n) (k : ℕ), (a ^ k).cast = a.cast ^ k
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {m : ℕ} [CharP R m], m ∣ n → ∀ (k : ℕ), (↑k).cast = ↑k
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {m : ℕ} [CharP R m], m ∣ n → ∀ (k : ℤ), (↑k).cast = ↑k
∀ {n m : ℕ} (h : m ∣ n), Function.Surjective ⇑(ZMod.castHom h (ZMod m))
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] [CharP R n], ZMod.cast 1 = 1
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] [CharP R n] (a b : ZMod n), (a + b).cast = a.cast + b.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] [CharP R n] (a b : ZMod n), (a * b).cast = a.cast * b.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] [CharP R n] (a b : ZMod n), (a - b).cast = a.cast - b.cast
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] [CharP R n] (a : ZMod n) (k : ℕ), (a ^ k).cast = a.cast ^ k
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] [CharP R n] (k : ℕ), (↑k).cast = ↑k
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] [CharP R n] (k : ℤ), (↑k).cast = ↑k
∀ {n : ℕ} (R : Type u_1) [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : CharP R n], Function.Injective ⇑(ZMod.castHom ⋯ R)

∀ {n : ℕ} (R : Type u_1) [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : CharP R n] [inst_2 : Fintype R],
  Fintype.card R = n → Function.Bijective ⇑(ZMod.castHom ⋯ R)

doc:
The unique ring isomorphism between `ZMod n` and a ring `R`
of characteristic `n` and cardinality `n`.
statement: {n : ℕ} → (R : Type u_1) → [inst : Ring R] → [CharP R n] → [inst_2 : Fintype R] → Fintype.card R = n → ZMod n ≃+* R

doc:
The unique ring isomorphism between `ZMod p` and a ring `R` of cardinality a prime `p`.

If you need any property of this isomorphism, first of all use `ringEquivOfPrime_eq_ringEquiv`
below (after `have : CharP R p := ...`) and deduce it by the results about `ZMod.ringEquiv`.
statement: (R : Type u_1) → [inst : Ring R] → [inst_1 : Fintype R] → {p : ℕ} → Nat.Prime p → Fintype.card R = p → ZMod p ≃+* R

∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : Fintype R] {p : ℕ} [inst_2 : CharP R p] (hp : Nat.Prime p)
  (hR : Fintype.card R = p), ZMod.ringEquivOfPrime R hp hR = ZMod.ringEquiv R hR

doc: The identity between `ZMod m` and `ZMod n` when `m = n`, as a ring isomorphism.
statement: {m n : ℕ} → m = n → ZMod m ≃+* ZMod n
∀ (a : ℕ), ZMod.ringEquivCongr ⋯ = RingEquiv.refl (ZMod a)
∀ {a : ℕ} (x : ZMod a), (ZMod.ringEquivCongr ⋯) x = x
∀ {a b : ℕ} (hab : a = b), (ZMod.ringEquivCongr hab).symm = ZMod.ringEquivCongr ⋯

∀ {a b c : ℕ} (hab : a = b) (hbc : b = c),
  (ZMod.ringEquivCongr hab).trans (ZMod.ringEquivCongr hbc) = ZMod.ringEquivCongr ⋯

∀ {a b c : ℕ} (hab : a = b) (hbc : b = c) (x : ZMod a),
  (ZMod.ringEquivCongr hbc) ((ZMod.ringEquivCongr hab) x) = (ZMod.ringEquivCongr ⋯) x
∀ {a b : ℕ} (h : a = b) (x : ZMod a), ((ZMod.ringEquivCongr h) x).val = x.val
∀ {a b : ℕ} (h : a = b) (z : ℤ), (ZMod.ringEquivCongr h) ↑z = ↑z
∀ {n : ℕ} (a : ZMod n), a.val = 0 ↔ a = 0
∀ (a b : ℤ) (c : ℕ), ↑a = ↑b ↔ a ≡ b [ZMOD ↑c]
∀ {n : ℕ} (a : ℤ) [NeZero n], ↑(↑a).val = a % ↑n
∀ (a b c : ℕ), ↑a = ↑b ↔ a ≡ b [MOD c]
∀ (a b c : ℕ), ↑a = ↑b ↔ a % c = b % c
∀ (a b : ℤ) (c : ℕ), ↑a = ↑b ↔ ↑c ∣ b - a
∀ {n : ℕ} (a : ℤ), (↑a).cast = a % ↑n
∀ {n : ℕ} (x y : ZMod n), (x + y).cast = (x.cast + y.cast) % ↑n
∀ {n : ℕ} (x y : ZMod n), (x * y).cast = x.cast * y.cast % ↑n
∀ {n : ℕ} (x y : ZMod n), (x - y).cast = (x.cast - y.cast) % ↑n
∀ {n : ℕ} (x : ZMod n), (-x).cast = -x.cast % ↑n

doc: `-1 : ZMod n` lifts to `n - 1 : R`. This avoids the characteristic assumption in `cast_neg`.
statement: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] (n : ℕ), (-1).cast = ↑n - 1
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {n : ℕ} (k : ZMod n), (k - 1).cast = (if k = 0 then ↑n else k.cast) - 1
∀ (p n : ℕ) (z : ZMod p) [NeZero p], ↑n = z ↔ ∃ k, n = z.val + p * k
∀ (p : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (z : ZMod p) [NeZero p], ↑n = z ↔ ∃ k, n = ↑z.val + ↑p * k
∀ (n : ℕ), (Int.castAddHom (ZMod n)).ker = AddSubgroup.zmultiples ↑n
∀ {m n : ℕ} [nzm : NeZero m], m ≤ n → Function.Injective ZMod.cast
∀ {m n : ℕ} [NeZero m], m ≤ n → ∀ (a : ZMod m), a.cast = 0 ↔ a = 0
∀ (p : ℕ) {z : ℤ}, 0 ≤ z → ↑z.toNat = ↑z
∀ (n : ℕ) [NeZero n], Function.Injective ZMod.val
∀ (n : ℕ), ZMod.val 1 = 1 % n
∀ (n : ℕ), ZMod.val 2 = 2 % n
∀ (n : ℕ) [Fact (1 < n)], ZMod.val 1 = 1
∀ {n : ℕ}, n ≠ 1 → ZMod.val 1 = 1
∀ {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a b : ZMod n), (a + b).val = (a.val + b.val) % n
∀ {n : ℕ} {a b : ZMod n}, a.val + b.val < n → (a + b).val = a.val + b.val

∀ {n : ℕ} (a b : ZMod n), (a + b).val ≤ a.val + b.val
∀ {n : ℕ} (a b : ZMod n), (a * b).val = a.val * b.val % n
∀ {n : ℕ} (a b : ZMod n), (a * b).val ≤ a.val * b.val
∀ {n : ℕ} {a b : ZMod n}, a.val * b.val < n → (a * b).val = a.val * b.val
∀ {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a b : ZMod n), (a * b).val = a.val * b.val ↔ a.val * b.val < n

doc:
The inversion on `ZMod n`.
It is setup in such a way that `a * a⁻¹` is equal to `gcd a.val n`.
In particular, if `a` is coprime to `n`, and hence a unit, `a * a⁻¹ = 1`.
statement: (n : ℕ) → ZMod n → ZMod n
∀ {n : ℕ} (a : ZMod n), a * a⁻¹ = ↑(a.val.gcd n)
∀ {n : ℤ}, ↑n = 0 ↔ Even n

doc: **Alias** of the reverse direction of `ZMod.intCast_eq_zero_iff_even`.
statement: ∀ {n : ℤ}, Even n → ↑n = 0
∀ {n : ℕ}, ↑n = 0 ↔ Even n

doc: **Alias** of the reverse direction of `ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff_even`.
statement: ∀ {n : ℕ}, Even n → ↑n = 0
∀ {n : ℤ}, ↑n = 1 ↔ Odd n

doc: **Alias** of the reverse direction of `ZMod.intCast_eq_one_iff_odd`.
statement: ∀ {n : ℤ}, Odd n → ↑n = 1
∀ {n : ℕ}, ↑n = 1 ↔ Odd n

doc: **Alias** of the reverse direction of `ZMod.natCast_eq_one_iff_odd`.
statement: ∀ {n : ℕ}, Odd n → ↑n = 1
∀ {n : ℕ}, ↑n ≠ 0 ↔ Odd n
∀ {n : ℕ} (x : ℕ), x.Coprime n → ↑x * (↑x)⁻¹ = 1
∀ {m n : ℕ}, m.Coprime n → ↑m * ↑(↑m)⁻¹.val = 1
∀ {m n : ℕ}, m.Coprime n → ↑(↑m)⁻¹.val * ↑m = 1

doc:
`unitOfCoprime` makes an element of `(ZMod n)ˣ` given
a natural number `x` and a proof that `x` is coprime to `n`
statement: {n : ℕ} → (x : ℕ) → x.Coprime n → (ZMod n)ˣ
∀ {n : ℕ} (x : ℕ) (h : x.Coprime n), ↑(ZMod.unitOfCoprime x h) = ↑x
∀ {n : ℕ} (u : (ZMod n)ˣ), (↑u).val.Coprime n
∀ (m n : ℕ), IsUnit ↑m ↔ m.Coprime n
∀ (m n : ℕ), (m % n).Coprime n ↔ m.Coprime n
∀ {n p : ℕ}, Nat.Prime p → (IsUnit ↑p ↔ ¬p ∣ n)
∀ {n p : ℕ}, Nat.Prime p → ¬p ∣ n → IsUnit ↑p

statement: ∀ {p d a : ℕ}, Nat.Prime p → 0 < d → (IsUnit ↑a ↔ ¬p ∣ a)

doc: In `ZMod (p ^ d)` with `0 < d`, the prime `p` is not a unit.
statement: ∀ {p d : ℕ}, Nat.Prime p → 0 < d → ¬IsUnit ↑p
∀ {n : ℕ} (u : (ZMod n)ˣ), (↑u)⁻¹ = ↑u⁻¹
∀ {n : ℕ} (a : ZMod n), IsUnit a → a * a⁻¹ = 1
∀ {n : ℕ} (a : ZMod n), IsUnit a → a⁻¹ * a = 1
∀ (n : ℕ) (a b : ZMod n), a * b = 1 → a⁻¹ = b
∀ {n : ℕ} {a : ZMod n}, IsUnit a → ∀ (b : ZMod n), a⁻¹ * b = 1 ↔ a = b

doc:
Equivalence between the units of `ZMod n` and
the subtype of terms `x : ZMod n` for which `x.val` is coprime to `n`
statement: {n : ℕ} → [NeZero n] → (ZMod n)ˣ ≃ { x // x.val.Coprime n }

doc:
The **Chinese remainder theorem**. For a pair of coprime natural numbers, `m` and `n`,
  the rings `ZMod (m * n)` and `ZMod m × ZMod n` are isomorphic.

See `Ideal.quotientInfRingEquivPiQuotient` for the Chinese remainder theorem for ideals in any
ring.
statement: {m n : ℕ} → m.Coprime n → ZMod (m * n) ≃+* ZMod m × ZMod n
∀ {n : ℕ}, Subsingleton (ZMod n) ↔ n = 1
∀ {n : ℕ}, Nontrivial (ZMod n) ↔ n ≠ 1
∀ {n : ℕ}, Odd n → ∀ {a : ZMod n}, a + a = 0 ↔ a = 0
∀ {n : ℕ}, Odd n → ∀ {a : ZMod n}, a ≠ 0 → a ≠ -a
∀ (a : ZMod 2), -a = a
∀ (a : ℤ), ↑a.natAbs = ↑a
∀ {n : ℕ} (a : ZMod n), a.val ≠ 0 ↔ a ≠ 0
∀ {n : ℕ} {a : ZMod n}, 0 < a.val ↔ a ≠ 0
∀ {n : ℕ}, 1 < n → ∀ (a : ZMod n), a.val = 1 ↔ a = 1
∀ {n : ℕ} (a : ZMod n), -a = a ↔ a = 0 ∨ 2 * a.val = n
∀ {n a : ℕ}, a < n → (↑a).val = a
∀ {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (a : ZMod m), a.cast.val < m
∀ {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : ZMod n), (-a).val = (n - a.val) % n
∀ {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : ZMod n), (-a).val = if a = 0 then 0 else n - a.val
∀ {n : ℕ} [nz : NeZero n] (a : ZMod n) [na : NeZero a], (-a).val = n - a.val
∀ {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {a b : ZMod n}, b.val ≤ a.val → (a - b).val = a.val - b.val
∀ {m n : ℕ} [nzm : NeZero m] {a : ZMod m}, a.val < n → a.cast.val = a.val
∀ {m n : ℕ} [hm : NeZero m], m ≤ n → ∀ (a : ZMod m), a.cast.cast = a
∀ {m n : ℕ} {a : ZMod n} [ilt : Fact (1 < n)], a.val ^ m < n → (a ^ m).val = a.val ^ m
∀ {m n : ℕ} [Fact (1 < n)] {a : ZMod n}, (a ^ m).val ≤ a.val ^ m
∀ (n : ℕ) (x y : ℤ), ↑x = ↑y → x.natAbs ≤ n / 2 → x.natAbs ≤ y.natAbs
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : NonAssocSemiring R] (f g : ZMod n →+* R), f = g
∀ {n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : NonAssocRing R] (f : R →+* ZMod n) (k : ZMod n), f k.cast = k

∀ (n : ℕ) (G : Type u_2) [inst : AddCommGroup G] [Module (ZMod n) G] [Nontrivial G], n ≠ 1

doc:
The range of `(m * · + k)` on natural numbers is the set of elements `≥ k` in the
residue class of `k` mod `m`.
statement: ∀ (m k : ℕ), (Set.range fun n => m * n + k) = {n | ↑n = ↑k ∧ k ≤ n}

statement: (N : ℕ) → [NeZero N] → ℕ ≃ ZMod N × ℕ
